From the surgery

Sick leave for psychological reasons

Sick leave can be necessary to recover, but it does not heal on its own. What it is for, what makes it useful and how to prepare the return.

By Alejandro Rosàs, family doctor

Anxiety, depression and stress reactions are among the most common causes of temporary sick leave. Taking leave for a mental health problem still makes many people feel ashamed, as if it were less legitimate than leave for back pain. It is not: when distress makes it impossible to concentrate, sleep or function at work, sick leave is part of the treatment.

What it is for

Sick leave serves to reduce a load that cannot be carried at that moment and to devote energy to recovery. It is not a holiday or a punishment, and it does not heal on its own. If it is spent at home, shut in and going over what happened, it can even worsen mood and make returning harder.

What makes it useful

  • Keeping a routine: regular sleep, meals and some daily activity.
  • Moving and getting out of the house, seeing other people.
  • Starting the agreed treatment: psychotherapy, medication or both.
  • Reviewing progress with the doctor regularly.

Preparing the return

Going back to work is often frightening, especially if the problem was related to it. It helps to think ahead about what has changed and what has not, what can be discussed with the employer or occupational health, and whether a gradual return is possible. Occupational health research shows that very long periods of leave without a return plan tend to become chronic. Going back, with support, is often part of recovery.

If the problem stems from conflict or bullying at work, sick leave protects health, but it is also worth seeking advice on how to resolve the underlying situation.

General information: it does not replace seeing a professional.
